'''''Phalaris brachystachys''''', the '''confused canary-grass'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''shortspike canarygrass''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PHBR3|taxon=Phalaris brachystachys|accessdate=23 September 2015}}</ref> is an annual grass with growth habits and cultural requirements similar to ''[[Phalaris aquatica]]''. It is native to the Mediterranean region. It grows most actively during the spring and fall, while resting during the heat of midsummer and the short cool days of winter. It also must be protected from heavy freezes.

Some ''Phalaris'' species contain [[gramine]], which can cause brain damage, other organ damage, [[central nervous system]] damage and death in sheep.<ref>
{{cite book
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eASgQyXq8xMC&q=%22mimosa+hostilis%22+dimethyltryptamine&pg=PA169

}}</ref>

While at least one strain showed an extremely strong occurrence of [[N,N-DMT]] as the sole alkaloid, other strains indicated the presence of [[5-MeO-DMT]] as well. Strongly positive human bioassays have been reported using some clones.<ref name="Ayahuasca: alkaloids, plants & analogs">[http://www.erowid.org/library/books_online/ayahuasca_apa/aya_sec3_part2_phalaris_strains.shtml Ayahuasca: alkaloids, plants & analogs]</ref>
